findings: The primary specimen is a convincing adult male Purple Finch: stocky and large-headed, with a compact conical bill, raspberry-red wash extending onto the back, brown wings, cloudy whitish lower belly, and no conspicuous dark flank streaking.
The rounded, softly puffy crown now agrees with Purple Finch structure in the references and avoids the pronounced crestlike peak associated with Cassin's Finch.

The primary specimen has one head, one bill, one visible eye, one tail, two convincingly attached legs with intact feet, and a complete wing pair with the far-side wing naturally occluded by the side-on pose.
The detached head and folded-wing studies read as intentional supplementary anatomy and do not appear attached to or duplicated on the primary specimen.
The bill proportions are compact and powerful in both depicted heads, without a truncated, reversed, or materially inconsistent mandible rendering.
The vertical body-length schematic increases correctly from 4.7 in (12 cm) at the bottom to 6.3 in (16 cm) at the top and is explicitly marked “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE.”
All displayed measurements exactly match Cornell's published both-sexes set: length 4.7–6.3 in (12–16 cm), weight 0.6–1.1 oz (18–32 g), and wingspan 8.7–10.2 in (22–26 cm).
The common name, scientific name, family, habitat, behavior, and field-mark text are legible and consistent with the proposed profile and the verified Cornell and Audubon accounts.
The palette labels match the depicted adult-male coloration and supporting neutral colors.
No place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, or local-observation detail appears.
